## Focus
- Readability and correctness of `reassemble_codex_turn`: the `getattr(item, "type", None)` dispatch, the `or ""`/`or {}` defensive defaults, the `item.tool` with `item.name` fallback. Are the defensive defaults sensible (codex SDK items vs fakes), or do they mask real bugs?

- Symmetry/consistency: `reassemble_codex_turn` produces blocks that `_parse_codex_message` consumes. Do their block shapes agree exactly (text: {type,text}; tool_use: {type,id,name,input})? Any drift between producer and consumer?
- Are the two tests meaningful? The reconstruct test is the real value — it exercises the actual audit API (reconstruct_request_for_response) end-to-end with a codex-shaped event stream. Does it genuinely prove tool_use/tool_result pairing (not a tautology)? Is the first test's exact-dict assertion appropriately strict?
- Placement: function sits between _serialize_mcp_result and _parse_codex_message — sensible grouping with the other codex render/audit helpers?
- Dead code / naming / magic values introduced by THIS change. (Note the function is intentionally uncalled in production — that is BY DESIGN, do not flag it as dead code; it's a latent guard with test callers.)
- Run `make typecheck` to confirm clean.
Note: pre-existing lint errors in docs/superpowers/spikes/ are NOT this commit's concern.

expected_findings.description: Three `# noqa: E402` imports appear after the first five tests with no explanatory comment; a separator comment would clarify intent and eliminate the code smell.
`FakeWebSearchItem` has no `id` attribute while the real SDK's `WebSearchItem` may have one, leaving the non-empty-id path untested; a note explaining this would clarify intent.
The filter `getattr(b, "name", None)` is an ad-hoc type discriminator; using `isinstance(b, ToolUseBlock)` would be tighter and more resilient.
